overlap.title: Overlap increases lexical and speaker-attribution errors.
overlap.description: Within-unit comparison of non-overlapped utterances and utterances with at least 50% overlap exposure.
overlap.control: Only inference units containing both classes are retained.

similarity.title: Speaker similarity is associated with pairwise confusion.
similarity.description: Spearman correlation between pairwise speaker similarity and pairwise confusion.

acoustic.title: Poor acoustic quality is associated with lexical errors and shorter predicted speech timelines.
acoustic.description: Correlation of acoustic degradation d_N with lexical error, attribution error, and hypothesized-to-reference speech duration ratio R_time.
acoustic.control: Computed on non-overlapping utterances away from speaker switches. R_time measures duration contraction, not boundary displacement.

turn.title: Speaker transitions primarily disrupt attribution.
turn.description: Within-unit attribution penalty in a +/-0.5 s neighborhood around non-overlapping speaker switches.
turn.control: E_lex and E_seg were not significant for any evaluated system.

speaker.title: Speaker number is associated with attribution difficulty after controls.
speaker.description: Partial correlation of speaker number and E_attr after controlling for dataset identity and overlap ratio.
speaker.control: P3 is excluded to reduce dataset-specific bias. Association does not imply causation; SoulX is not evaluated.
